A finite-group average rules out every strict quadratic unless a>gamma; odd leading degree cannot be globally positive. The supplied exact symbolic verifier reconstructs polynomial identities from actual equations. Finite examples are diagnostic only.

value.rationale: The phase-locked angular region has distinct invariant rays and a sharp global sink-to-neutral/outward transition. A uniform explicit quartic SOS certificate works even when the Euclidean radial energy grows on open sets, and the exact minimum strict polynomial degree jumps from 2 to 4. This settles a natural precise fixed-degree certification question for a canonical symmetry-reduced cubic normal form, not a generic low-value parameter substitution.
